dimensions.evidence: Observed x86-64 GCC/Clang DSCopyView16, DSCopyOps16, DSMulti40, bytes receiver offset8, scalar value offset32 and DSCaptureSpec24 bytes; DSDeferred160, token16 and OwShared32. Rust1.93.1 measured a zero-sized marker and16-byte trait reference. These are target observations, not C or Rust ABI promises.

The length/copy wrapper owns16 staging bytes. Borrowed views retain no owner storage; the owner and tables must remain live. A deferred binding retains one actual T66 shared-owner reference and one stationary pthread control, with externally allocated thread-stack/OS resources additional.

Borrowed subobjects expire with their enclosing object and must be reconstructed after interface-table changes. Deferred environments stay retained from bind through worker completion and actual join; cancellation is not quiescence. Tokens use generations1..3 then retire4.

Two borrowed interfaces observe the same enclosing live object through different typed receiver addresses. The controller owns deferred state transitions; worker predicates/results use one mutex. Reentry and copying active pthread controls are outside the contract. Runtime wrappers cannot validate arbitrary dangling pointers.

Copy laws, subobject adapters and admission policy allocate nothing. Accepted owning captures delegate to actual T70 storage and actual T66 allocator; rejected self-reference, over-alignment and borrowed-return requests fail before allocation. Deferred retention can fail before mutation when dead or saturated.

Copy stages at most16 bytes, checking promised and observed lengths before publishing. A valid self-reference counterexample keeps both old/new typed objects live and demonstrates why byte relocation preserves the wrong internal pointer; a typed repair explicitly updates it. No arbitrary-object relocation guarantee is offered.

Deferred drain joins first, clears control ownership and advances/retire generation before releasing the retained T66 owner. The last shared drop invokes destruction/release exactly once. Queue cancellation skips the body; running cancellation permits the body to finish but suppresses publication.

Length and copy each run once for admitted requests, including empty requests. Type-correct callbacks can violate the relation or produce wrong content; independent content oracles remain necessary. Retained closures invoke one typed body through a borrowed callback and owning environment protocol.

Five actual pthread schedules exercise queued/running cancellation, failed calls, join/drain and one-time ownership release. GCC TSan instruments the seven-profile semantic campaign. No scheduler fairness, all-interleaving proof, lock-free progress or pthread-cancel cleanup guarantee follows.

102 independent copy rows and34 direct measure comparisons distinguish callback errors, capacity and count-law violations.59049 explicit closure transitions plus extrema/copied-state examples exercise local consumption. Explicit admission rejects unsupported alignment/relocation/return-lifetime requests; the return-type constraint has a compiling positive control.

The probe records actual GCC/Clang O2 builds, linked programs, disassembly and stack reports. Rust1.93.1 accepts the type-correct wrong semantic implementation, and separately diagnoses E0053, E0046, E0599, E0515 and E0382. A move capture whose body only reads remains callable repeatedly. No general Rust/C safety equivalence follows.
